content: The Prince of Wales Hospital, located in Sha Tin in the New Territories of Hong Kong, is a public hospital that also serves as the teaching hospital for the Faculty of Medicine at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. Established in 1984, the hospital is equipped with approximately 1,360 beds and operates a 24-hour accident and emergency department. It employs nearly 4,000 staff members to provide comprehensive medical services. The hospital functions as the regional medical center for the Eastern New Territories, catering to the healthcare needs of residents in Sha Tin, Tai Po, North New Territories, Sai Kung, and the outlying islands in the region. The Prince of Wales Hospital gained international attention, albeit controversially, during the SARS outbreak in Hong Kong. Specialty outpatient services at the hospital are supported by the Li Ka-shing Specialist Clinics, which provide advanced and focused medical care. The ultimate decision-making authority for the hospital is the Hospital Governing Committee (HGC). The current Chief Executive of the Prince of Wales Hospital is Dr. Fung Hong. The hospital was named in honor of Charles, Prince of Wales.
